Description:
Problem:
When a repository has multiple remotes, the CLI note explaining where checkpoints are synced was incomplete and misleading. It stated that checkpoints "follow whichever remote you push to" and "always look at origin," but didn't explain which specific remote was actually elected as the sync destination—especially when the election is still open and depends on which remote receives the first push.
Solution:
The code now queries the actual elected checkpoint sync remote and displays it by name in the status note. It explains three scenarios: (1) when a remote is pinned via checkpoint_push_remote setting, (2) when the branch's declared push destination has been elected, and (3) when no election has happened yet and the first push to the branch's push destination will elect it. The changes remove misleading phrases and replace them with accurate descriptions of the current destination and how it gets selected.

content.text:
Both tests pass. Review of trail 1108 (`fix/checkpoint-destination-note-capture`, 2 commits over `cmd/entire/cli/remote_topology.go` + tests):

## Verdict
The core change is right — asking `strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` instead of re-deriving from settings is exactly the `CoreOrigin()` rule from CLAUDE.md, and per-tier wording is a genuine accuracy win over "follow whichever remote you push to". Three things I'd fix before merge.

## 1. The `syncErr` invariant comment is false, and there's a silent output gap
`remote_topology.go:60-67` claims a failed election is "the only reason `syncRemote` can be empty where the note is written". It isn't. `ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` returns `{}, nil` when `configuredRemotesInConfigOrder` comes back empty (`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:104`), and that helper swallows read errors: `cachedRemotesInConfigOrder` returns `nil` on a transient `git config` failure (`git_remote_cache.go:194-198`) precisely so the failure isn't cached.

So on a transient git failure (fork failure under load, cancelled ctx, locked config), the note prints:

```
  This repo has 2 remotes (backup, origin).
  To pin one repository for checkpoints, set checkpoint_remote in
```

…and says nothing at all about where checkpoints go — strictly less than the old static text. Either make `describeSyncRemote` fall back to a tier-agnostic sentence when both `syncRemote` and `syncErr` are empty, or drop the claim and accept silence deliberately. As written the comment asserts an invariant the code doesn't hold.

Related, smaller: the two remote listings don't come from the same command — the note counts remotes via `git remote -v` (`pushURLsByRemote`), the resolver via `git config --local --get-regexp` (which excludes non-local scopes). They can disagree, which is also the loophole in the "`Sole` cannot occur here" comment at `remote_topology.go:250`. The `Sole` wording is shared with `First` so nothing breaks; just don't state it as impossible.

## 2. Dropping "no session history" loses the most actionable fact for settled elections
The commit rationale for asserting `"no session history"` absent is that it's untrue for the push that elects a remote. That's true only for the *open* tiers (`Default`/`First`). For `Config` and `Observed`, `captureEligible` returns false immediately (`checkpoint_sync_capture.go:158-161`), so no push can move the election, and "a push to any other remote carries your code but no session history" was exactly correct — and it's the one thing a multi-remote user needs to know. The new note tells them the destination but never that the other remote drops their transcripts. I'd restore a scoped version on the two settled tiers rather than deleting it repo-wide.

## 3. "your first push … takes it over" is a no-op in the common case
On the `Default` tier the elected remote is `origin`; if the branch's declared push destination is also `origin` (the ordinary setup), `captureEligible` bails on `elected.Name == pushRemote` and no takeover ever happens. The sentence promises a change that can't occur for most readers. Something like "a push to a different remote of your own can move it" would be true in both shapes.

## Smaller notes
- `inspectRemoteTopology` now resolves the sync remote unconditionally, including when `ambiguous()` is false and nothing is printed. One extra `settings.Load` + subprocess on `enable`/`doctor` only — fine, not worth changing.
- `SyncRemoteSourceFirst` has no test case (it's folded into the `Default` arm). Cheap to add given the table is already there.
- The `Observed` wording ("your branch's push destination") is repo-wide captured state, not per-branch, so it can be wrong on a branch that pushes elsewhere — but it matches `status.go:359` verbatim, so leave it unless you change both.

content.text:
All three fixes are in, `mise run fmt` clean, lint 0 issues, `./cmd/entire/cli/...` unit tests and `TestMultiPushURL*` integration tests pass.

**1. Silent gap on an unreadable election** — `describeSyncRemote` now has a third branch: name empty *and* no error means the resolver's own `git config` read failed transiently, so it prints `Checkpoints sync to a single elected remote; \`entire status\` shows which.` rather than nothing. The `syncErr` field comment no longer claims a failed election is the only way the name can be empty; it names `cachedRemotesInConfigOrder`'s nil-on-transient-failure as the other path.

**2. "no session history" restored on the settled tiers** — emitted for `Config` and `Observed`, where `captureEligible` refuses every displacement so no push can move the destination; still absent on the open tiers, where the electing push itself would make it false. The doc comment explains that split.

**3. Takeover wording** — the open-tier arm now reads:

```
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — right now "origin". A push to a different
    remote of your own can move it; `entire status` shows where they go.
    Set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to pin one yourself.
```

"a different remote" instead of "your branch's own remote", since capture requires the target to both agree with the declared push destination *and* differ from today's election — so on the common setup where they already agree, nothing moves.

**Smaller notes** — added a `SyncRemoteSourceFirst` table case; the "Sole cannot occur here" comment is downgraded to "all but unreachable", with the reason (the caller and the resolver count remotes with different git commands). Left `inspectRemoteTopology`'s unconditional resolve and the `Observed` per-branch wording alone, as discussed.

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push
- Always show the user what was committed and the PR URL when done

it, so a repo with two remotes could print its remote count and then say
nothing at all about where checkpoints go — strictly less than the static
text this replaced. Fall back to the one clause true on every tier.

"A push to any other remote carries your code but no session history" was
dropped repo-wide because the electing push disproves it. It only does so
on the open tiers; with checkpoint_push_remote set or a capture in force,
captureEligible refuses every displacement, so the sentence is exactly
right there — and it is the fact a multi-remote user most needs. Restore
it on those two tiers only.

"your first push to your branch's own remote takes it over" promises a
move that cannot happen in the ordinary setup: capture needs the target to
both agree with the declared push destination and differ from today's
election, so when they already agree, no push moves anything.

## The problem

The several-remotes note printed by `entire enable` / `entire doctor` says:

> Checkpoints sync to a single elected remote — not to whichever one you push to. **A push to any other remote carries your code but no session history.** Run `entire status` to see the elected destination and how many checkpoints are waiting for it.

That bolded sentence is not true of the one push that matters most. `pendingCaptureCheckpointSyncRemote` runs **before** the single-remote gate in `prePush`, so a push whose target agrees with the branch's declared push destination elects that remote *and* carries the checkpoints there in the same push (`TestCheckpointSyncRemote_TrackedPushCapturesElection` asserts exactly that). The note was warning about a case the CLI now handles by itself.

It also never said where checkpoints actually go — the one thing a user standing in a multi-remote repo wants to know.

## The change

`inspectRemoteTopology` asks `strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` for the election (never re-derived from settings — the same rule the existing `pinned` field follows, so the shown destination cannot diverge from where pushes go), and the note says the concrete thing. Election still open:

```
  This repo has 3 remotes (custom, origin, upstream).
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — right now "origin", and your first push to
    your branch's own remote takes it over. `entire status` shows where.
    Set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to pin one yourself.
```

Observed tier — destination settled, capture clause gone:

```
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — "custom", your branch's push destination.
    Set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to pin a different one.
```

Explicit `checkpoint_push_remote` — one line, no advice, because repeating the key they already set reads as a warning that something still needs doing:

```
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — "custom" (set by checkpoint_push_remote).
```

Fourth state: the election failed. Where this note is written there are always at least two remotes, and a successful election over two or more remotes always returns a name — so an empty name means the resolver failed closed on a `checkpoint_push_remote` that names a remote which does not exist, and checkpoints are going nowhere at all. The error is kept on the topology rather than swallowed into a debug log, and reported in the wording `entire status` already uses:

```
    Checkpoints are NOT syncing: checkpoint_push_remote "gone" is not a configured git remote; checkpoint sync disabled until fixed
```

That is the only branch here that is a warning rather than orientation, and it was the one previously printing nothing at all.

The fan-out block above (one remote, several push URLs) is untouched — that one is still genuinely lossy.

The tier switch names the three open tiers instead of falling through to `default`: golangci-lint's `exhaustive` rule rejects the default clause. `SyncRemoteSourceSole` is unreachable at this call site — this note is written only when two or more remotes are unpinned, and the resolver reaches the sole tier only with exactly one remote configured — so it is grouped with the open tiers under a comment saying so, plus what to do if that gate ever loosens ("your first push takes it over" is meaningless with one remote).

## Test

`TestMultiPushURL_DestinationNoteSurfaces` asserts `"no session history"` **absent**, alongside the two phrasings this note was already wrong with (`"follow whichever remote"`, `"always looks at origin"`), so a future rewrite cannot reintroduce any of the three.

`TestDescribeSyncRemote` (new, `cmd/entire/cli/remote_topology_test.go`) covers every tier the note words differently — config, observed, open election, fail-closed, and nothing-resolved — asserting both the text that must appear and the text that must not, since the integration test only ever reaches the open-election tier. `describeSyncRemote` is a pure function of two fields and an `io.Writer`, so the table is cheap.

- `mise run test` → 9313 tests, 4 skipped, 0 failures (186s).
- `TestMultiPushURL` (integration, all cases) and `TestDescribeSyncRemote` pass.
- All four states verified by hand against a 3-remote repo.
